newsitem.title: ITALY: Cuban sugar recovering from hurricane - minister.
newsitem.headline: Cuban sugar recovering from hurricane - minister.

text.p: Cuba is recovering from a recent hurricane and still aims to improve on last year's sugar harvest despite the damage it wreaked, food industry minister Alejandro Roca Iglesias said on Thursday.
Hurricane Lili ripped through central and western areas of Cuba in October, damaging crops, destroying more than 5,000 homes and cutting power lines and communications.
"We will have more than last year," Roca told Reuters on the margins of a Rome summit. He declined to elaborate.
Last year's harvest was 4.45 million tonnes, he said.
"There was a cyclone recently which caused some damage but I thought that the plans we had forecast for the next sugar cane harvest could be achieved in spite of this damage," he said.
"The country is recovering from the damage of this cyclone and is in a process of accelerated recuperation," he said.
He was speaking during a break on the second day of a five-day U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit, where Cuban leader Fidel Castro is expected to arrive later this week.
Roca said he could not confirm Castro's schedule.
Cuban vice-president Carlos Lage said in late October that despite damage caused by the hurricane, Cuba could still improve on last year's sugar crop, its economic lifeline.
In an interview with the Communist Party newspaper Granma, Lage noted that affected crops included some 670,000 hectares of sugar cane, just months ahead of the start of the 1996-97 harvest.
But he said that although cane was flattened or flooded, much of it would be usable.
Before the hurricane, sugar experts had said Cuba could produce around 5.2 million to 5.3 million tonnes of sugar.
Last year's harvest of around 4.5 million tonnes marked the halt of a steady decline in Cuba's key export earner since the early 1990s.
Production in 1994-95 was a disastrous 3.3 million tonnes, the lowest harvest on the island for 50 years.
